Sex distribution for the Madagascar cohort (54 female, 58 male) is an aggregate count, not assignable to a single subject-level enum value under this schema.
No explicit disease/condition target is described; the study investigates microbiome diversity across age, geography, and lifestyle rather than a specific clinical condition.
The paper does not report per-sample identifiers, per-subject ages, or antibiotic exclusion criteria in the provided text.
Lifestyle classification ('Agriculturalist') for the Madagascar cohort is inferred from a description of diet (self-grown rice) rather than explicitly stated using the schema's enum terms.
Batch 1 subgroups ['newborn', 'children', 'school-age', 'adult', 'adult_and_senior'] differ from batch 0 ['Madagascar cohort', 'Ethiopian cohort']; kept batch 0.

This paper is a large-scale metagenomic genome reconstruction/microbiome diversity study, not a clinical cohort study; the vast majority of schema fields (disease, treatment, tumor staging, obgyn, neonatal clinical details, HLA, zygosity, etc.) are not applicable/not reported.

Age information is reported as discrete age categories (newborn, children, school-age, adult, adult-and-senior) with sample counts across 46+ meta-analyzed studies plus Madagascar/Ethiopia cohorts, rather than as individual participant ages; age_min/age_max were derived per age-category subgroup rather than per participant.

There appears to be an internal inconsistency in the text regarding the 'adult' vs 'adults and seniors' age category boundaries (one sentence gives adults as 19-65 years with 6,615 samples, another gives 'adults and seniors' as ≥19 and >65 years with 876 samples); this could not be fully resolved from the text.
The 'disease' field's by_subgroup uses cohort-based subgrouping (Madagascar/Ethiopia) which differs from the main age-category subgrouping declared at the top level; flagged for reviewer attention.

Overall study includes non-Westernized cohorts (Madagascar, Ethiopia) explicitly enrolled and described in STAR Methods, while the bulk of the 9,428 metagenomes come from 46 previously published external datasets for which most participant-level clinical/demographic details beyond age category, body site, and country are not provided in this paper.
